title: Normalize sentence-shaped concept records into their constructions

example.spanish: De ahora en adelante, llama primero.

candidates.rationale: Sentence demoted to the example; the concept is the fixed time expression the row was filed under (adelante).
Concept is the preposition, not the sentence. Distinct from the bare additive adverb además.

example.english: It is expensive; moreover, it is far away.

candidates.rationale: Third distinct English target for además, alongside also and besides.
Source file names this target: ante (… above all).
Source file 06-hardly-context. Teaches casi no => hardly, not the literal almost not.

candidates.english: can hardly wait for [something] to happen
candidates.rationale: Source file 10-hardly-wait. The Spanish never contains apenas; the mapping is idiomatic.

example.english: He was tired; even so, he went out.

candidates.rationale: Concept is the concessive connector.
Latin American variant of detrás de, which already exists separately.

example.english: Years ago, I lived in Cali.

candidates.rationale: Variant of hace [un período de tiempo]; the postposed atrás form.

example.english: All it takes is one call.

candidates.rationale: Concept is the bastar con construction.

candidates.english: all you need to do is [do something]

example.spanish: Basta con leer el primer párrafo.
example.english: All you need to do is read the first paragraph.

candidates.rationale: The verb-complement form of bastar con.
Formal concessive connector; aunque already covers the everyday register.

example.english: Either you study or you work.

candidates.rationale: Correlative bien...bien; rare in Latin American Spanish, kept at reference.
Parallel Spanish route to had better alongside mas vale [hacer algo].
Concept is the discourse marker.

example.english: What can I help you with?

candidates.rationale: Teaches Spanish fronted preposition vs English stranded preposition.
Informal stranded form; the formal to whom variant is a separate row.
Formal fronted-preposition register, deliberately split from the stranded form.

example.english: Which book do you want, this one or that one?

candidates.rationale: Source file 01-which-limited-choice.
The cual-is-not-which trap: Spanish cual maps to English what here.
Question frame; the bare interrogative cuándo is held separately in core.

example.english: How long have you been here?

candidates.rationale: Question frame for duration.
Literary cuán; the everyday Colombian form is qué tan.
Parallel to the con que and con quien stranding rows.

example.spanish: Trabajo de noche y descanso de vez en cuando.
example.english: I work at night and rest from time to time.

candidates.rationale: Original row bundled de noche and de vez en cuando; de noche is already covered by por la noche, so this keeps the uncovered half.

example.spanish: Temblaba de frío y lloraba de alegría.
example.english: She was shaking with cold and crying with joy.

candidates.rationale: Source file 03-cause-and-reaction: de marks cause, English uses with.

example.spanish: El resultado depende de Ana y de que el sistema funcione.
example.english: The result depends on Ana and on the system working.

candidates.rationale: The clause-complement form; depender de [algo] already exists.
Future-time dentro de.

example.english: You must respond within the deadline.

candidates.rationale: The boundary sense, distinct from the future-time sense.

example.english: Starting tomorrow, we will open earlier.

candidates.rationale: Starting-point sense of desde.

example.spanish: Desde mi punto de vista, es correcto.
example.english: From my point of view, it is correct.

candidates.rationale: Fixed opinion phrase.
Fixed agreement expression.
Question frame; bare donde is held in core.

candidates.spanish: entre más [ocurre algo], más [ocurre otra cosa]
candidates.english: the more [something happens], the more [something else happens]

example.english: The more you practice, the more you learn.

candidates.rationale: Latin American entre mas correlative; the more...the more construction.

example.english: There are more than one hundred people.

candidates.rationale: More-than with numbers, where Spanish uses de rather than que.

example.spanish: Está en medio de la calle.
example.english: It is in the middle of the street.

candidates.rationale: Concept is the locative phrase.
Exception sense of menos.

example.spanish: Ana cocina, mientras que Luis limpia.

candidates.rationale: Source file 02-whereas: contrastive, not temporal, mientras.
Source file 07-by-oneself.

example.spanish: Trabajo mucho entre semana, pero descanso los domingos.
example.english: I work a lot during the week, but I rest on Sundays.

candidates.rationale: Adverbial mucho modifying a verb.

example.spanish: Tenemos mucho tiempo; no hay que apurarnos.
example.english: We have plenty of time; there's no need to rush.

candidates.rationale: Plenty-of sense of mucho.

candidates.english: neither [to do something] nor [to do something else]
candidates.rationale: Verb-phrase neither/nor.
Noun-phrase neither/nor, distinct from the verb form.
Siquiera as even in a negative clause.
The ni siquiera intensifier.

example.english: Give me at least five minutes.

candidates.rationale: Positive at-least sense of siquiera.
The Spanish nunca to English ever swap in questions.
Question frame for why.

example.spanish: Terminó más pronto de lo esperado.

candidates.rationale: Fixed comparative phrase.
Standard sense of de pronto.
Colombian sense of de pronto; a genuine regional split from suddenly.

example.english: At what time does it start?

candidates.rationale: Question frame for clock time.

example.spanish: Asegura que la puerta esté cerrada.

example.spanish: No solo vino, sino que ayudó.

candidates.rationale: First half of the split correlative; one teachable unit per row.

example.spanish: No solo vino Laura, sino también Mateo.
example.english: Not only Laura but also Mateo came.

candidates.rationale: Second half of the split correlative, taking over the previously bundled row.
Source file 03-except: sino as but/except.

example.english: Whenever she calls, I am busy.

candidates.rationale: Temporal whenever sense.

example.english: You can call me whenever/as long as you want.

candidates.rationale: Conditional sense; the original English bundled whenever/as long as into one field.
